subject: OpenTelemetry → Datadog adapter: technical eligibility triage and go/no-go gating
messages:
From: Alex Hughes <alex.hughes@datadog.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@grafana.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick check — OTel adapter eligibility for Datadog ingestion

Vivek,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. We ran the basic compatibility scan on our side and have a few gating items before we can commit to co-packaging an official Datadog ingestion adapter:

- Supported OTLP encodings (protobuf/grpc vs http/protobuf) — we saw some older agents using http/json.
- High-cardinality label handling — we need a proposed downsampling/label-strategy.
- Backpressure behavior over sustained bursts (30–60s spike) — we need a sample trace or traffic CSV.

Can you share the traffic profile (p95 payload size, typical spans/sec per service) and the draft eligibility checklist you mentioned? If we clear these technical gates we'll route this to commercial for co-sell packaging.

Thanks,
Alex Hughes
Partner Solutions Engineer — Datadog

- Grace: can you run the traffic sample through our pre-cert harness and produce p50/p95/p99 metrics + a short readout by EOD Friday?

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Quick check — OTel adapter eligibility for Datadog ingestion

Vivek / team,

Quick technical note (summary for Alex):
- Backpressure / queueing: our adapter uses an async bounded queue with token-bucket send rate. Under sustained bursts we apply adaptive dropping at 0.75 * queue_capacity for noisy label groups; important metrics emitted so customers can opt-in to stricter cardinality trimming.
- Retries: 3 attempts with exponential backoff, circuit open for 30s after 5 consecutive 5xx responses.
- Encoding: we support grpc/protobuf and http/protobuf; legacy http/json is converted via a lightweight normalization pipeline (adds 6–8ms median overhead).
- High-cardinality strategy: we expose a labels-policy config (hashing prefixes, prefix-truncation, and histogram-binning). We recommend applying policy default for Datadog co-packaged SKU.

I'll attach a 1-pager and mock config snippet to the checklist. Ben

Attachments: partner-sow-template.docx

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpenTelemetry → Datadog adapter: technical eligibility triage and go/no-go gating

Hi all — jumping in from Grafana's side to confirm a couple items that affect packaging:

- If Redwood's adapter normalizes http/json -> protobuf, will Grafana Cloud's ingestion accept the same normalized payload or do we need a separate translation layer? (Alex, would be great if Datadog can confirm.)
- Co-sell collateral: Grafana would like a joint architecture diagram and a 1-page "what's included in the adapter" doc.

Observify (copied) suggested a short joint lab test to exercise a 1M spans/hour sustained burst — we can do that next week if Datadog has lab capacity.

Sarah Li
Strategic Alliances — Grafana

Subject: Re: OpenTelemetry → Datadog adapter: technical eligibility triage and go/no-go gating

Thanks everyone — quick status update:

- Technical: Ben's note looks good. The encoding/queueing approach fits our ingestion model.
- Lab run: we have lab windows next Tuesday; Observify please confirm test harness and schedule.
- Commercial: Laura, if technical lab passes, Datadog is willing to proceed to a joint listing and a shared partner SKU with a 70/30 revenue split (Datadog 70) for year one.

Next steps agreed:
1) Observify to schedule lab (end of week).
2) Grace to post lab readiness snapshot to the Drive folder (p50/p95/p99).
3) Laura and Alex to exchange draft term sheet; Laura will send an initial commercial term email by EOD Thu.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looks like a path to sign off.

Alex Hughes
Partner Solutions Engineer — Datadog
